extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, representatives/attorneys, and EPO examiners/practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Official EPO examination Guidelines describing procedural and substantive requirements for drafting, prosecuting, examining and opposing European patent applications and patents under the European Patent Convention and its Implementing Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the European Patent Convention and Implementing Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines give instructions on the practice and procedure to be followed in the various aspects of the examination of European applications and patents in accordance with the European Patent Convention and its Implementing Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines are authoritative instructions to ensure examination and related procedures comply with the EPC and Implementing Regulations; amendments reflect legal and procedural developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the latest valid version of the Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to the frequent revisions, you are advised to use the online version, which always publishes the latest valid version in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The November 2014 edition is the only valid official version and supersedes the September 2013 edition as from 1 November 2014. Online HTML/PDF show modifications and are recommended over printed copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination (Part A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part A describes the procedures for formalities examination in grant and opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers formal requirements and the procedural steps to check compliance with formal rules during grant and opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search matters (Part B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part B deals with search matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on how searches should be conducted as part of European patent prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural aspects of substantive examination (Part C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part C relates to procedures to be followed in substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains instructions for examiners and parties on the conduct of substantive examination of patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition and limitation/revocation procedures (Part D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part D relates to procedures to be followed in opposition proceedings and limitation/revocation procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rules and practice to be followed when opposing a granted European patent or in limitation/revocation cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: General procedural matters (Part E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part E deals with procedural matters relevant to several or all of the stages in procedure at the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes cross-cutting procedural issues and information concerning the Euro‑PCT procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements other than patentability (Part F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part F defines the requirements which the application must fulfil other than patentability, such as unity, sufficiency, clarity and the right to priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F sets out formal and substantive non-patentability requirements that applications must meet under the EPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (Art. 82)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention (Art. 82) is a requirement an application must fulfil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F explains the assessment of unity and related procedural consequences under Article 82 EPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure (Art. 83)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficiency of disclosure (Art. 83) is required so the invention is disclosed sufficiently for a skilled person to carry it out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F explains how sufficiency is evaluated and what constitutes adequate disclosure under Article 83 EPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (Art. 84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity (Art. 84) of claims and specification is a formal requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F provides guidance on assessing clarity and claim drafting requirements under Article 84 EPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to priority (Arts. 87–89)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to priority (Arts. 87 to 89) is defined and explained as a requirement for European applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F includes rules and procedural practice concerning priority claims and proof of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (Part G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part G deals with the requirements of patentability provided for in Arts. 52 to 57, in particular exclusions from patentability, novelty, inventive step and industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G details substantive patentability assessment criteria and their application under the EPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from patentability (Art. 52(2) and Art. 53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions from patentability as provided for in Art. 52(2) and Art. 53 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G explains which subject-matter is excluded from patentability (e.g., certain discoveries, mathematical methods, etc.) and relevant tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Art. 54)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty (Art. 54) — the invention must be new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G explains how novelty is assessed against the prior art and what counts as disclosure under Article 54 EPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (Art. 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive step (Art. 56) — the invention must involve an inventive step (non‑obviousness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G provides guidance on how to assess inventive step and apply problem‑solution approaches or other relevant tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial application (Art. 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial application (Art. 57) — the invention must be capable of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G explains criteria for industrial applicability and examples of how to assess it under Article 57 EPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements relating to amendments and corrections (Part H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part H defines the requirements relating to amendments and corrections, in particular questions of admissibility and compliance with the EPC provisions and Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers admissibility under Rules 80/137, added‑matter and extension issues under Art. 123(2)/(3), and correction rules (Rules 139/140).

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of amendments (Rule 80 and Rule 137)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions of admissibility of amendments under Rule 80 and Rule 137 are addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H explains when and how amendments are admissible in the grant and opposition phases and the procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Article 123(2) and (3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with Art. 123(2) and (3) — prohibition of added subject‑matter and extension of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H provides guidance on assessing added subject‑matter (no new matter) and that amendments must not extend the protection conferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections under Rule 139 and Rule 140
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections under Rule 139 and Rule 140 concern the correction of errors in documents and miscellaneous corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H explains the scope and procedures for correcting errors in applications and patents under the specified Rules.
